# Northstar — Monday Business Review: What the Data Actually Supports

**Prepared by: Product & Growth Lead | Period: Sept–Oct 2026 (both months complete)**

---

## 1. EXECUTIVE SUMMARY

- **October's headline revenue growth is mostly an illusion.** As loaded, October shows €892.9k vs September's €797.1k (+12.0%). But €19.5k of that is a **duplicate invoice** (INV-2026-10-0209, soylent, loaded from both `stripe` and `billing_sync`), and gringotts' €120k annual prepayment covers 12 months. On a monthly-equivalent MRR basis (plans.csv), recurring revenue grew **€746.1k → €757.7k = +1.6%**.
- **The real story is churn:** 5 customers and **€303.6k ARR (3.3% of opening ARR)** lost in October — 1 mid-market (nakatomi, €180k) and 4 SMB (€123.6k). All five were 12–26 months tenured, and all showed usage declines of −16% to −37% *before* churning. Enterprise: zero churn.
- **Acme's −45% request drop is the planned batch migration** (estimate was 40–50%). Tokens fell only −12%; active users −3%. Not a health signal.
- **paid_search's headline attributed revenue (€274.8k) is 76% expansion credit** from existing enterprise customers whose usage was already growing ~10%. Its new-logo yield per lead (€46) is the lowest of any channel; partner's is €1,236.
- **The CFO's CAC-payback request cannot be answered from this pack** — there is no channel spend data anywhere in it.
- **Plan economics:** pro is strongest (62.7% margin, visible friction/monetization signals); enterprise holds 79% of plan profit but margin compressed 32.2% → 29.5% on support costs; starter is weakest (support = 32% of revenue; 4 of 13 customers churned).

**Bottom line on the three decisions:** (1) No segment cut is supported — SMB needs a retention fix, not disinvestment. (2) Do not scale paid_search on this evidence. (3) Pro plan gets the engineering focus, with enterprise reliability as a protected parallel track.

---

## 2. REVENUE & CUSTOMER HEALTH

### What is driving the headline numbers

| View | Sept | Oct | Δ |
|---|---|---|---|
| Invoiced, as loaded | €797,100 | €892,900 | +12.0% |
| Deduplicated (remove 2nd soylent invoice) | €797,100 | €873,400 | +9.6% |
| MRR, monthly-equivalent (plans.csv) | €746,100 | €757,700 | **+1.6%** |

**Bridge from Sept €797.1k to Oct €892.9k (+€95.8k):**
- +€19.5k duplicate soylent invoice (data error)
- +€110k gringotts annual invoice booked at full value vs €10k monthly equivalent (€120k ÷ 12)
- +€11.6k genuine MRR growth
- −€45.3k professional services decline (€51.0k → €5.7k; lumpy, not recurring)

**Genuine MRR bridge (+€11.6k):** +€11.1k from 5 new logos (all SMB: spacely 3.2k, gekko 2.2k, cogswell 2.1k, paper-street 1.9k, bishop 1.7k) + €3.0k hooli expansion (the Sept-attributed €36k landing on cycle) − €2.5k soylent downgrade (€22.0k → €19.5k).

**November will mechanically step down.** October's invoices include €25.3k MRR from customers who churned mid-October (nakatomi 15.0k, buy-n-large 3.3k, mega-lo-mart 2.7k, dinoco 2.3k, slate-rock 2.0k) because billing is in advance. Offsetting this, October's expansion bookings (€216k ARR: stark 84k, umbrella 48k, globex 42k, cyberdyne 24k, massive-dynamic 18k) take effect next cycle = **+€19.5k/month from November**. Net: November MRR opens around **€751.9k**, slightly *below* October — a mechanical dip, not new deterioration.

### Churn — the number that matters

- Opening October ARR: €9,092.4k (active €8,788.8k + churned €303.6k). October ARR churn = **3.3% monthly (~40% annualized — treat with caution, n=5, one month)**.
- By segment: **Enterprise 0%** | Mid-market 10.5% (nakatomi) | **SMB 20.5%** (4 of 18 customers).
- Pattern: every churner was 12–26 months tenured, and every one showed a usage decline in the churn month: nakatomi −16.1%; slate-rock −34.7%; mega-lo-mart −37.1%; dinoco −35.5%; buy-n-large −37.0%. **A ~−35% MoM usage decline is a reliable leading indicator in this data.**

### Health signals

- **Enterprise demand is fine:** 7 of 8 accounts grew requests +5–10%. Aggregate tokens processed grew **+5.6%** (32.1B → 33.9B) even though total requests rose only +1.9% (ex-acme: **+9.3%**).
- **Soylent is the top at-risk account (€234k ARR):** usage −27%, a price downgrade, and 8 October tickets including the pack's only *critical* (api_errors). Tickets went 3 → 8 MoM.
- **Wayne Enterprises (€1.008M) renews 30 November** — in ~5 weeks — with an open high-severity api_errors ticket and pending high-severity performance ticket. Usage is +10% and above quota (renewal upside, but delivery risk).
- **Acme:** −45% requests is within the migration plan's 40–50% estimate; tokens −12%, users −3%. Expected.

---

## 3. ACQUISITION

### What can be concluded

| Channel | Leads S→O | Paid trials S→O | Trial rate S→O | New-logo ARR (2 mo) | New-logo ARR per lead |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| paid_search | 520→900 (+73%) | 44→58 (+32%) | 8.5%→6.4% | €64,800 (2 logos) | **€46** |
| content | 260→330 | 31→34 | 11.9%→10.3% | €91,200 (3) | €155 |
| partner | 60→75 | 15→17 | 25.0%→22.7% | €166,800 (2) | **€1,236** |
| outbound | 160→195 | 10→11 | 6.3%→5.6% | €56,400 (2) | €159 |

- **paid_search is showing classic diminishing returns:** leads +73%, trials +32%, and the *marginal* trial rate on the incremental 380 leads is 14/380 = **3.7%** — less than half the September base rate. Scaling it further is buying volume at declining quality.
- **Attribution decomposition (total credited €631.2k):** paid_search credits €274.8k, but **€210k (76%) is expansion** from stark, umbrella, globex (all 2023–24 vintage, usage already growing ~10% before the Sept 28 campaign start) plus hooli. The platform credits expansion at conversion; **nothing in this pack shows paid search caused it**. By contrast, partner delivers €166.8k — 100% new logo, including the only quality logo of the period (vandelay, €132k, mid-market).
- **No channel produced a single enterprise new logo in two months.** All 9 new logos are SMB (8) or mid-market (1). Enterprise growth is entirely expansion-led — more acquisition spend will not move enterprise ARR.

### What cannot be concluded

- **CAC, ROI, or CAC payback by channel** — no spend data exists in the pack. The CFO's request cannot be fulfilled from this data.
- **Trial→paid conversion** — explicitly not tracked; funnel "conversions" are paid *trials*, not customers. 220 trials produced 9 visible new logos, but lag effects make even that comparison unreliable.
- October's paid_search trials (58) have not yet had time to convert; judging the channel on same-month logos understates it. The two-month view above partially smooths this, but the yield gap (€46 vs €1,236 per lead) is too large to be a lag artifact alone.

---

## 4. PLAN ECONOMICS (cost-adjusted)

| Oct | Customers | Revenue | Infra | Support | **Profit** | **Margin** | Sept margin |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| enterprise | 14 | €659,500 | €296,800 | €168,000 | **€194,700** | **29.5%** | 32.2% |
| pro | 9 | €66,200 | €16,100 | €8,600 | **€41,500** | **62.7%** | 67.5% |
| starter | 13 | €32,000 | €11,400 | €10,300 | **€10,300** | **32.2%** | 34.9% |

- **Enterprise is the profit pool (79% of total plan profit, 87% of MRR) but margin fell 2.7pp in one month**, driven entirely by support cost (+€9k with flat customer count) — consistent with the chronic high-severity api_errors/performance tickets at stark, wayne, contoso. Note: plan customer counts include mid-month churners, so per-customer figures are slightly conservative.
- **Pro is the strongest plan on margin (62.7%)** despite a 4.8pp dip (support +25% during onboarding of new customers). Critically, pro shows a **packaging mismatch**: 3 of 9 customers exceed the 600k included requests — **wonka at 1.02M (170% of quota), aperture 705k (118%), vandelay 690k (115%)** — and pro-plan rate-limit tickets exploded from 4 to 13 MoM. That overage is billable *at renewal* (wonka Mar-27, aperture Apr-27, vandelay Sep-27) but the rate isn't in the pack, so the upside can't be sized in €.
- **Starter is the weakest:** support cost is 32% of revenue (€792/customer/month vs €2,462 ARPU), absolute profit is trivial (€10.3k/month), and 4 of 13 starter customers churned. Starter customers use only 42% of their quota on average — no monetization upside, real retention risk.
- **Enterprise quota watch:** stark at 143% of included requests (4.29M vs 3.0M) and wayne at 114% — both up from September. Overage lands at renewal; wayne's is 30 November.
- **Acme pricing dynamic to monitor:** quota is request-based but cost tracks tokens. Acme's requests fell −45% while tokens fell only −12% (tokens/request rose 1.1 → 1.76 with batch jobs). Enterprise infra cost rose +3.1% MoM despite requests falling — batch migrations improve the customer's request economics faster than our cost base.

**Verdict:** strongest = **pro**; weakest = **starter**; enterprise = largest profit pool with eroding margin from support costs, plus near-term overage upside at renewals.

---

## 5. RECOMMENDATIONS

**1. Segment investment (Finance): No reduction is supported this week.**
- Enterprise (77% of active ARR, zero churn, usage +5–10%): protect, don't cut.
- Mid-market: keep investing; launch a save motion on soylent (€234k at risk) this week.
- SMB: do **not** cut — it supplied 8 of 9 new logos and net SMB ARR still grew ~€125k over two months despite the churn spike. The problem is *retention*, not acquisition: all four SMB churners showed −35% usage declines first. Implement a usage-decline trigger (alert at −30% MoM) and a save playbook for tenured accounts. If budget must be reduced, take it from paid_search spend aimed at SMB (lowest per-lead yield), not from the segment. Note: segment-level P&L **cannot be computed** from this pack (costs are tagged by plan, not segment) — request that allocation before any structural decision.

**2. Channel spend (Growth): Do not increase paid_search.**
- Its headline is an attribution artifact (76% expansion credit, causality unsupported) and its marginal trial conversion is 3.7%. If incremental budget is released, run **bounded tests in partner** (best logo quality: €83.4k avg ARR) **and content** ( steadiest trial rate, 10–12%), conditional on instrumenting channel spend first.
- Fix attribution reporting: split new-logo vs expansion credit. The €216k expansion ARR booked in October lands in Nov/Dec invoices — the highest-ROI action is **protecting those six accounts**, not buying more demand.

**3. Plan focus (Product): Pro gets the quarter.**
- Scope: overage metering and billing, rate-limit UX (tickets 4→13, all pro), and an enterprise upgrade path for wonka / aperture / vandelay. This converts an evidenced friction point into renewal revenue on the highest-margin plan.
- Non-negotiable parallel track: enterprise reliability (api_errors/performance) — 79% of profit depends on it, margin fell 270bps, and wayne (€1.008M) renews in ~5 weeks with an open high-sev ticket.
- Starter: no engineering investment; retention playbook only.

**4. CFO CAC payback:** Cannot be produced from this data. Interim deliverable: new-logo ARR per lead by channel (above) plus plan gross margins (29.5% / 62.7% / 32.2%) as the payback denominator. Commit to full payback = CAC ÷ monthly gross profit per logo once channel spend is loaded into the funnel file. Use new-logo ARR only — exclude expansion credit.

**5. Data hygiene (this week):** remove the duplicate soylent invoice (dedup on transaction_id); publish October both as-billed and MRR-normalized; enforce joins on `usage_account_id` (wayne_ent, prestige_ww differ from customer_id — a naive join silently drops **€1.122M ARR, 12.8% of active ARR**); filter `status='churned'` when summing arr_eur (all 35 rows still carry ARR).

---

## 6. UNCERTAINTIES / DATA ISSUES

1. **Duplicate invoice:** INV-2026-10-0209 (soylent, €19.5k) appears twice (stripe 10-01, billing_sync 10-02). Inflates October by 2.2%.
2. **Annual prepayment distortion:** gringotts €120k covers 12 months; reading invoices as monthly revenue overstates October by €110k. MRR view is the correct lens.
3. **Advance billing + mid-month churn:** €25.3k of October MRR belongs to customers who already left; November will show a mechanical decline. Do not misread as deterioration.
4. **CAC/payback by channel: not calculable.** No spend data exists; funnel conversions are paid trials, not customers; trial→paid is untracked.
5. **Attribution causality is unsupported,** especially expansion credit (paid_search: €210k of €274.8k). Expansion revenue is also not yet billed (next cycle) and is not yet in arr_eur.
6. **plans.csv counts include mid-month churners** (pro = 9 includes nakatomi; starter = 13 includes 4 churned), so per-customer plan metrics are slightly diluted; plan revenue includes €25.3k from churned accounts.
7. **Segment P&L impossible:** infra/support costs are tagged by plan, not segment; mid-market spans two plans. The "reduce segment investment" decision cannot be evaluated on profitability — only on health signals.
8. **Overage revenue cannot be sized:** included quotas are known; the overage rate is not.
9. **Acme's −45% is explained** (planned migration, 40–50% estimated). But the request-based quota vs token-based cost mismatch is a structural pricing watch item as workloads shift to batch.
10. **Support data limits:** month-scoped tickets with a status snapshot; no aging, no resolution times; September "open" items may since have resolved. Backlog direction (19 → 24 unresolved) is indicative only.
11. **Small sample:** one month of churn (n=5), two months total; annualized churn (~40% ARR) and channel yield-per-lead figures are directional, not stable rates. New-customer usage growth (e.g., vandelay +33%) reflects onboarding ramp, not trend.
12. **No enterprise new logos in the window,** so channel performance for enterprise acquisition is untestable from this data.
